# When custom USD terrain causes severe divergence in human training results on two identical GPUs, can we directly attribute it to the drive?

> **Current answer:** Cannot. The original maintainer requested alignment of the drive, but subsequent analysis, based on results from approximately two thousand steps prior, suggested it was not a simple drive issue. The current approach should prioritize checking the host drive, the course/condition triggers in the vicinity of this step, and custom terrain representation, while preserving the PVD log. The original post has not yet provided a final root cause.

## Key terms

- Training Non-Determinism (训练非确定性)
- Whole-Body Control (WBC) (全身控制)
- Physics Visual Debugger (PVD) (物理可视化调试器)

## Problem and symptoms

- The same code, container, and GPU model produced qualitatively different human training results on two machines.
- Local training can learn the mimic, but the cloud robot cannot stand; the default plane and built-in terrain generator do not trigger.

## Environment

- Isaac Lab 2.1, Isaac Sim 4.5, RTX 4090, whole_body_tracking, custom USD terrain.

## Priority diagnostics

- Aligned the host drive, compared random seed distributions, and checked for course/condition triggers in the vicinity of approximately two thousand steps; the PVD log was preserved.

## Possible causes

- Custom terrain representation may alter contact modeling or contact resolution, but the root cause has not been confirmed.

## Attempts

- The author compared the default plane, built-in terrain, and custom USD, and recorded the PVD from the first 100 iterations.

## Result

- The maintainer is still investigating; no final fix has been verified.

## Limitations

- This issue cannot prove that the drive version or custom terrain is the root cause; it can only indicate variables to be checked.

## Safety notes

- Do not rely on a single training curve to assess deployment reliability; compare multiple statistical measures and final task metrics.

## Image and visual evidence

- The training curve comparison for this issue is used to show the divergence after two thousand steps; the current round did not perform pixel-wise coordinate reading, and the time point judgment comes from the maintainer's textual analysis of the divergence in the vicinity of two thousand steps.

## Applicability boundary

- Applicable to training that involves a rich variety of cross-machine contact; cannot be generalized to all Isaac Lab training that is not reproducible.
